The Lift Spectrum

Image-free sensing can be more robust to measurement noise than reconstructing an image first.

The Lift Spectrum: How Measurement-to-Space Adaptivity Shapes Robustness in Image-Free Single-Pixel Sensing

Yuyuan Han, Jingwei Li, Xiaoxia Zhang, Long Qiu, Chong Wang, Wenxuan Hao, Jiangyu Han, Xinyu Yao, Yuchen He, Hui Chen, Jianbin Liu, Huaibin Zheng

Source: § IV-D, Fig. 4
Comparison conditions

Foreground mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) measures segmentation overlap with background excluded. The chart shows differences in percentage points. STSF is the image-free network; TPLS is task-prioritized loss scheduling.

All headline models were trained on clean data. Each scene has 128 × 128 pixels and 512 natural-order Hadamard measurements (3.13% sampling). The noisy condition uses 20 dB additive Gaussian measurement noise calibrated on the AC-coupled bucket signal.

The values are foreground mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) differences in percentage points, reported over three training seeds. Each condition uses its strongest tested reconstruction-first baseline. The clean values reverse the sign of the paper’s reported baseline lead so that every row follows the same subtraction.

This comparison uses the paper’s fixed acquisition and normalization. Noise-aware retraining can restore reconstruction-first performance near the training calibration; see Table III in the same section.

Contribution & evidence

  • Robustness: direct inference overtakes the strongest tested reconstruction-first baselines as measurement noise increases, when all models are trained on clean data.
  • Representation: a content-adaptive 1D-to-2D lift turns the measurement sequence into spatial task features.
  • Training: task-prioritized loss scheduling (TPLS) shifts emphasis from auxiliary reconstruction to the sensing task.

One shared measurement source

Synthetic input without added perturbation.

Reconstruct → segment

An image is the intermediate representation.

Image reconstruction

Receives the measurement sequence and measurement model. Passes an estimated two-dimensional image to the task network.

Image-to-task inference

The segmentation head reads the reconstructed image. In this study, it is adapted to the images produced by the reconstruction method.

Image-free segmentation

The task head reads features formed from measurements.

Content-adaptive 1D-to-2D lift

Cross-attention maps the encoded measurement sequence into two-dimensional task features. Their spatial organization is adapted to the measurement content.

Task representation

The segmentation head receives spatial task features. Auxiliary reconstruction supplies training supervision; its reconstructed image is not the segmentation input.

Task-prioritized loss scheduling

Auxiliary reconstruction helps establish structure early in training. The schedule then increases the priority of the segmentation task.
